body:
I think this was done on purpose, as [per-pixel roughness is not supported when using per-vertex shading](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ab98cb9c1bd7fbe7ee70a8d71bcbca4a1e49b7e6/scene/resources/material.cpp#L1207-L1212) (unlike per-pixel metallic, which does work somehow). If it was possible to use ORMMaterial3D with per-vertex shading, then the roughness map would appear to have no effect and you'd be stuck with full roughness.

**Edit:** It seems per-pixel roughness *does* work partially when using vertex shading in StandardMaterial3D, but only on lighting contribution that is still being performed on a per-pixel basis (such as reflection probes). Direct light is not affected (e.g. specular lobes), as seen in this video:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/30f97a07-3adf-46aa-b7ee-b10a9fb1ec97

**Testing project:** [test_per_vertex_roughness.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32938288/test_per_vertex_roughness.zip)

> Also a new ORM material appears to be darker in the preview than a new Standard Material.

This is because the fallback ORM texture is white, which means a newly created ORMMaterial3D is fully metallic (instead of being fully dielectric like a StandardMaterial3D).

To resolve this, we'd need to add `hint_default_yellow` (or a way to have a custom color) and use it as a fallback for the ORM texture when it's not set.
